behaviorVerified: Capture whether the exact Popen child was unreaped at function entry. An entry-already-reaped child cannot obtain another group probe from this recovery path.
Keep the initial exact-child poll and group signal-zero probe. A denial can obtain at most one fresh probe only after that exact child has newly acquired a confirmed returncode during this call.
Newly confirmed reap by the initial poll, the post-denial poll, or one exact-child wait is accepted as lifecycle evidence. The source is recorded as a fixed enum.
Only when both polls still leave the entry-unreaped child unreaped, allow one process.wait(timeout=0.05). A timeout rethrows the original PermissionError with timeout exception context suppressed.
An unconfirmed returncode after wait cannot authorize a fresh probe, even if a test double returns an exit code. Unexpected wait failures remain fail-closed.
A newly reaped child merely authorizes a fresh group query. Fresh False is authoritative group absence, fresh True remains alive, and fresh denial/error remains unverified and propagates.
No additional signal, role exclusion, process target, privilege, resource measurement, retry count, resource limit or unknown-to-zero conversion is introduced.

Fixed-schema cleanup diagnostics record entry reap availability, observed exact-child exit codes, reap result/source, optional bounded-wait seconds and whether a fresh probe was attempted. They include no raw PID, UID, command, output or exception text and retain the existing latest-16 bound.
Timeout diagnostics use wait-timeout rather than claiming a kernel running state. A child cannot be declared gone by timeout alone.

AST comparison after removing only Runner.owned_group_alive confirms the remainder of support.py is unchanged from the parent, including inventory retries, resource handling, first failure, excerpts, stage records and independent final leader wait.
The only other changed files are cleanup tests. Plan, SDK transport/content pins, Darwin counter validation, native discovery/ownership, pipeline, harness and Runtime workflows are unchanged.
limits: The historical run13 group denial cause is unknown. This patch covers call-local exact-child lifecycle windows without identifying the original denied state.

The first-poll reap precedes the first denied group query, so its acceptance does not itself explain why a second group query would improve. Only the fresh query result establishes current group state.
The 0.05-second exact-child wait is bounded and may still time out under real scheduling conditions; such timeout intentionally preserves the denial.

A controlled injected denial establishes the recovery-path mechanics, not reproduction of the historical kernel denial. Twenty successful rapid stops would not by themselves prove that the historical race occurred during those iterations.
Original native exit, inventory helper delay and compiler causes remain unknown. Actual native authentication has not been tested by this review.
No new Mac job, full build, SDK acquisition, repository source modification or external write was performed by this review.

negativeAndBoundaryCoverage: Initial-poll new reap followed by fresh False, True or EPERM preserves the fresh result without waiting.
Post-denial-poll new reap permits one fresh probe.
Bounded-wait new reap followed by fresh False, True or EPERM preserves the fresh result.
Live child wait timeout rethrows the same original denial and does not query the group again.
Entry-already-reaped child neither waits nor gains a recovery probe.
Wait success without a confirmed returncode does not permit a recovery probe.
Group denial and denied signals retain primary monitor failure, unverified cleanup and independent exact-child final wait.
